speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To understand your weakness and decreased sensation in the right arm, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they came on suddenly or gradually? Have you noticed any numbness spreading to other parts of your body or any trouble speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use, alongside progressive weakness and weight loss, I need to rule out compression neuropathy or a systemic metabolic issue. Can you describe the exact location of the numbness and whether you have any neck pain or muscle atrophy? REQUEST TEST: HbA1c, CBC, CMP, TSH.

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs confirm uncontrolled diabetes with elevated glucose and abnormal liver enzymes, which aligns with your history. Given your weight loss, chronic alcohol use, and steroid use, we must urgently rule out paraneoplastic syndrome or an infiltrative process. Can you pinpoint exactly where the weakness and numbness are located in the right arm, such as the hand, forearm, or shoulder? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine, CT Chest.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your progressive weakness, sensory loss, and pain in the right arm, combined with significant weight loss and your history of steroid use, we need to determine if this is a peripheral nerve issue like a brachial plexopathy or a central spinal cord issue. Can you describe the specific pattern of weakness (e.g., can't lift your arm, grip weakness) and does the pain radiate from your neck or shoulder down the arm? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of anabolic steroid use, heavy alcohol consumption, and significant weight loss, I am concerned about a paraneoplastic process or an infiltrative tumor affecting your brachial plexus or cervical spine. Have you noticed any visible wasting of the muscles in your right arm or shoulder compared to the left? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine with contrast, CT Chest.
